title: Multi-Level Sales Commission
description:
Commission rules: reps earn **5% of their own sales**; a manager (has reports and also has a manager) earns **2% of direct reports' sales**; the top of the tree (manager_id IS NULL) earns **1% of everyone else's sales**. People can earn more than one component.

**Table: people** — `id`, `name`, `manager_id`, `sales`

Output columns: `id`, `name`, `commission`. Order by `id`. Round to 2 decimals.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE people (id INT, name VARCHAR, manager_id INT, sales DECIMAL(10,2)); INSERT INTO people VALUES (1,'VP',NULL,0),(2,'Mgr A',1,0),(3,'Mgr B',1,0),(4,'Rep 1',2,1000),(5,'Rep 2',2,500),(6,'Rep 3',3,800);
solution_sql: SELECT p.id, p.name, ROUND(p.sales * 0.05 + CASE WHEN p.manager_id IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM people c WHERE c.manager_id = p.id) THEN (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(sales), 0) FROM people WHERE manager_id = p.id) * 0.02 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN p.manager_id IS NULL THEN (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(sales), 0) FROM people WHERE id <> p.id) * 0.01 ELSE 0 END, 2) AS commission FROM people p ORDER BY p.id

test_cases.description: VP 23, Mgr A 30, Mgr B 16, Rep1 50, Rep2 25, Rep3 40

hints: Detect mid-level managers with EXISTS on children AND manager_id IS NOT NULL; the VP is the NULL manager_id row.
explanation: Reps: 5% of 1000/500/800 = 50, 25, 40. Mgr A: 2% of 1500 = 30. Mgr B: 2% of 800 = 16. VP: 1% of 2300 = 23. Leaf nodes have no 2% term because they have no reports.
